title: WHAT STEPPING OFF SAVES
subtitle: A 1 GW flexible compute load at ERCOT's 14 hubs and load zones: off at the four summer peaks and at or above USD 1,000 per MWh, against a flat load

inputs_words.profile: Flexible compute: 0.90, off in ERCOT's four summer peaks and at or above USD 1,000 per MWh

All-in at HB_HUBAVG, USD per MWh, flat and flexible

why: A 1 GW load that steps off in ERCOT's four summer peak intervals and in every hour at or above USD 1,000 per MWh gave up 5 to 15 hours of the last twelve whole months, row by row, and paid USD 8.60 (LZ_SOUTH) to USD 10.78 (LZ_CPS) per MWh less all-in than a flat load at the same row. At HB_HUBAVG: USD 32.50 against 42.38. Most of the saving is the four-peak transmission charge, which a load off at the four peaks does not pay; the rest is the dearest hours' energy. All-in is energy over the hours the load runs, the four-peak charge at the Commission's rate, and capacity, of which ERCOT has none.
footnote: Data: the All grids tab of "What a datacenter pays" (/cost-of-power?view=allgrids&profile=flexible&mw=1000), computed by site/lib/siting.ts from the page's own files: the hourly hub and zone prices (ercot_all_hub_prices_history, ercot_zone_prices_history), ercot_4cp_intervals and the Commission's approved rate (texas_transmission_matrix). Method: docs/methods/siting.md. The replication: warehouse/replication/siting.py.
source_line: Source: ERW, the All grids tab (/cost-of-power?view=allgrids&profile=flexible), from ERCOT's hourly prices and four-peak intervals and the PUCT's transmission matrix.
